newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: World airports report lower passenger, cargo growth.
newsitem.headline: World airports report lower passenger, cargo growth.

text.p: World airports reported slower growth in passenger traffic and air cargo freight in February after a good start in January, the Geneva-based Airports Council International (ACI) said.

The ACI, which links 486 international airports and airport authorities in more than 150 countries, said air passenger traffic grew by 2.7 percent in February over a year ago, down from January's 6.5 percent growth rate.
Cargo growth reported by world airports slumped to 4.5 percent in February over a year ago from January's jump of 12 percent, it said in a statement.

Africa led the growth in passenger traffic in February with 21.5 percent. Passenger traffic growth was also buoyant in the Asia Pacific region with 6.5 percent and in Europe with 5.6 percent but flat in North America.
Cargo growth was highest in Asia Pacific region with seven percent, followed by North America with 4.6 percent, Europe with 3.4 percent and Africa with 2.3 percent.
